Grokking

Test performance improves long after training performance has saturated. Power et al., 2022 ↗

GeneralizationOptimization

Claims

SupportsLimitsChallenges
V1Algorithmic models can generalize long after memorization, with longer delays on smaller datasets 1621044

Suggested status R2independently reproduced

Several independent groups reproduce transitions from chance to near-perfect test accuracy after training accuracy levels off in transformers and ReLU networks. Using smaller training fractions delays generalization in experiments with a fixed task, but these findings depend on the task, optimizer, architecture and evaluation split.

Original resultPower et al., 2022 ↗

Power et al. trained small transformers on division modulo 97 and on composing permutations (S5).

With 50% of modular-division data, training accuracy approached perfection before 10³ steps, while validation accuracy approached perfection near 10⁶ steps. Near 25–30% training data on S5, a 1% decrease increased median time to exceed 99% validation accuracy by 40–50%.

Main discussion, Dmitry’s clarification of the meaning of grokking

Related findings5 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Data and capacity separate learning regimes 25 studies

Data coverage and model capacity can separate memorization, delayed generalization and immediate generalization. Such thresholds can arise without explicit weight decay.

  • Polynomial regression shifts from failed generalization to grokking to simultaneous learning as P increases. Tanishq Kumar et al., 2023 ↗
Structure and sampling shape generalization 25 studies

Algebraic structure, input representation and sampling affect whether and when generalization occurs. Training-set size alone does not determine whether held-out examples are recoverable.

  • Recursive feature machines fail on test points unchanged by reflection; repartitioning training/test data restores high accuracy. Marcelo Bernal et al., 2026 ↗
Generalization can appear, disappear and return 12 studies

Rules and transferable solutions can appear before memorization and later be displaced by memorization or competing priors. Capability changes can reverse during training.

  • OLMo3-32B Successive Answer answer+1 accuracy falls from 81% to zero before recovering to 81.7%. Jia-Xin Wen et al., 2026 ↗
Label noise changes the path to generalization 8 studies

Label noise can delay or block grokking and change the order of fitting clean and corrupted labels. Recovery depends on corruption structure, optimization history and which labels are corrected.

  • Uniform training-label noise delays grokking, with measurable effects even at 0.5% noise. Havish Singavarapu, 2025 ↗
Fewer updates need not mean greater efficiency 5 studies

Acceleration measured in updates need not improve sample or compute efficiency. Dataset-size effects depend on whether updates, epochs, examples or FLOPs are held fixed.

  • Batch size 512 reaches the threshold within the step budget, not the example budget. Roland Y. Fang, 2026 ↗
V4Grokking-like delayed generalization occurs during language-model pretraining and fine-tuning 571

Suggested status R2independently reproduced

Several independent groups report grokking-like delayed generalization during language-model pretraining and fine-tuning, using different measures. Evidence is task-dependent, and scales above 10B parameters remain unresolved.

§5, “Sustained, not instantaneous”

Related findings3 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Model design controls the delay 24 studies

Architecture, initialization, parameterization and training objectives can shorten, remove or prevent delayed generalization. Learning need not shift from keeping features near their initial values (lazy learning) to changing them substantially (rich learning).

  • On synthetic KG-QA, shared-access configurations cross the OOD threshold across seeds while Dense never crosses. Ya-Nan Niu, 2026 ↗
Task structure and supervision can shorten delays 11 studies

Task-compatible representations, symmetries and intermediate supervision can shorten or remove grokking. Incompatible structural constraints can prevent it.

  • For COMPARISON, k=3 Max, ϕ=3.6, CoT supervision advances OOD take-off from 120K to 16K steps. Zihan Pengmei et al., 2025 ↗
Delayed generalization extends beyond standard neural settings 6 studies

Delayed generalization also occurs in linear, kernel and matrix-completion settings. Neural feature learning, adaptive optimizers, softmax and explicit weight decay are not universal requirements.

  • Multiplication-table matrix completion minimizes training loss long before its sharp test-loss transition. Kaifeng Lyu et al., 2023 ↗

How it works

V2Gradual circuit formation, then removal of memorizing components, can underlie grokking 74553

Suggested status Ccontested

Several independent groups find internal progress before grokking, but gradual circuit formation followed by removal of memorizing components remains disputed as a general explanation. Some circuits or probe measurements change only during generalization, and larger-model studies support only parts of this explanation.

Original resultNanda et al., 2023 ↗

The study tracked loss using only selected Fourier frequencies, sparsity (concentration at fewer Fourier frequencies), and squared weights in a one-layer transformer learning addition modulo 113.

Loss restricted to key Fourier frequencies fell before test loss, which dropped suddenly after circuit formation as memorizing components were removed. In this later phase, Fourier sparsity increased sharply and the decline in squared weights sped up.

Related findings6 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Abrupt learning without prior memorization 37 studies

Abrupt capability gains can occur without prior memorization or a gap between training and test performance. Features can develop before these gains, either without visible performance changes or in stages.

  • Online-trained transformers filling matrix gaps stall at copying, then learn abruptly without a training–test performance gap. Pulkit Gopalani et al., 2024 ↗
Representation geometry changes around grokking 22 studies

Representation rank, dimension, clustering and topology can change around grokking. The direction and timing of these changes depend on the task, architecture and measurement.

  • Last-layer LLID drops with the validation-accuracy jump and reaches lower minima in grokking runs. B. Brown et al., 2022 ↗
Internal development continues after accuracy saturates 16 studies

Representations and circuits can keep simplifying, reorganizing or becoming transferable after task accuracy saturates. This later development need not involve delayed behavioral generalization.

  • T5-Base grammar transfer reaches 90% relative performance 48k steps after in-task performance reaches that level. Shengnan An et al., 2023 ↗
Gradient allocation shapes generalization 12 studies

Gradient direction, competition that prevents some features from learning, and interactions between modules affect grokking. The evidence does not support a universal shift from MLPs memorizing to attention generalizing.

  • Boosting non-commutativity accelerates Dyck grokking, while a kick prevents SCAN grokking. Yongzhong Xu, 2026 ↗
Initialization helps determine which features survive 7 studies

Initialization and the frequency content of input encodings partly determine which generalizing features survive training. They also influence the order in which Fourier components are learned.

  • Fourier-circle survival correlates with initial signal, and perturbing that signal changes survival. Xiaoman Delores Ding et al., 2024 ↗
Generalizing structure can coexist with memorization 5 studies

Subnetworks, masks or frequency filtering can recover generalizing structure from models that also memorize. Sparsity alone does not explain this recovery.

  • Filtering frequency components post-training recovers near-perfect test accuracy under 80% label noise, without establishing delayed generalization. Lin-Yu Liu et al., 2026 ↗
V5Weight decay favors efficient generalizing circuits over memorization 71554

Suggested status R0claimed in one paper

Small algorithmic experiments link circuit efficiency (generalizing with smaller weights) to a threshold dataset size and to loss of generalization after reducing data. Independent groups reproduce regularization’s contribution to generalization, but the full explanation that weight decay favors efficient generalizing circuits over memorization has not been independently reproduced.

Original resultNanda et al., 2023 ↗

The study varied training data and weight decay in one-layer transformers learning modular addition.

The study argued that weight decay favors a Fourier circuit with smaller weights over memorization, while squared weight norm fell as the circuit formed and memorizing components were removed. With modulus 113, 10% or 20% training data produced no grokking after 40k epochs, whereas 30–50% did.

Related findings2 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Total weight norm leaves important differences unresolved 21 studies

Weight norm can affect how long grokking takes, but its trajectory alone is insufficient to explain it. How norm is distributed across layers, activation scale, saturation of pre-softmax outputs (logits) and weight direction also matter.

  • Redistributing fixed norm between embedding and output layers changes grokking time despite similar pre-softmax output scale. Xuan Khanh Truong, 2026 ↗
Regularization can govern the delay before generalization 20 studies

In some regimes, grokking delay follows a clock involving learning rate and decay strength. Excessive regularization and feature learning limit this relationship.

  • Weight decay applied during only some training steps preserves modular-addition generalization but delays grokking about fivefold. Sarwan Ali, 2026 ↗
V6Networks trained on the same task converge to the same algorithm 26306

Suggested status Ccontested

Models trained on modular addition and sorting can learn different algorithms depending on architecture, initialization or seed, challenging the claim that all runs converge to the same algorithm. Independent groups find that related algorithms recur under specific conditions, while Pythia models of different sizes show broad consistency in their algorithms but differences in their components.

Original resultNanda et al., 2023 ↗

The study reverse-engineered one-layer transformers trained on addition modulo 113 using 30% of examples.

The main model used Fourier multiplication at five key frequencies; four other random seeds used the same algorithm with different frequencies. Across varied data fractions, depth, prime moduli, and regularization, every correctly generalizing model trained with weight decay reportedly implemented a variation of Fourier multiplication.

Answer-only Loss

Answer-only Loss

standard transformers · Train first with answer-only loss, then with full-sequence loss · Loss schedule: answer-only until 100% accuracy, then full-sequence until convergence

V7Do optimizer and numerical artifacts fully explain the grokking delay? 4416

Suggested status Ccontested

The claim that controlling optimizer behavior and numerical effects eliminates grokking delays is contested. Delays persist under plain gradient descent and precision controls, while stabilizing numerical calculations can enable delayed grokking.

Original resultNanda et al., 2023 ↗

The study compared grokking with slingshot behavior (repeated sudden loss spikes late in training) in 1-layer transformers with regularization.

Many 1-layer models grokked without slingshots (repeated sudden loss spikes late in training), showing that slingshots are unnecessary for grokking with weight decay or other regularization.

Appendix C.2, Figure 42

Related findings3 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Optimization changes speed and reliability 23 studies

Optimizer dynamics and regularization affect grokking timing and reliability. Acceleration methods can interfere with one another or trade speed for stability.

  • SNR-gated Adam reaches 95% held-out accuracy 4.9× faster than AdamW. Elon Litman et al., 2026 ↗
Loss spikes do not uniquely explain generalization 8 studies

Slingshot loss spikes and optimizer oscillations can accompany changes in learned representations and improved generalization. Spikes alone neither predict grokking nor establish a unique beneficial mechanism.

  • On sparse parity, slingshots and matched random perturbations produce loss improvements with no statistically significant difference. Wilson Wu, 2024 ↗
Numerical choices can change individual outcomes 4 studies

Finite-precision choices can cause loss spikes or change individual grokking outcomes. Aggregate grokking rates can remain unchanged despite these differences.

  • Reordering how CPUs combine results or switching CPU/GPU flips individual grokking outcomes without detectable overall-rate shifts. Yoshiyuki Ootani, 2026 ↗

Stability and robustness

These studies test whether generalization persists through continued training, perturbations and new data.

Generalization can deteriorate after grokking 11 studies

Generalization can relapse or collapse during continued training. Stability depends on optimizer updates, regularization, numerical effects and subsequent data.

  • Modular-addition test accuracy declines after grokking while training accuracy remains perfect. Hari Prakash et al., 2026 ↗
Accurate solutions can differ in robustness 5 studies

Robustness can develop after clean generalization and differ between equally accurate solutions. Behavioral grokking alone does not establish resistance to perturbations or forgetting.

  • After noise memorization, WLMD-equilibrium models retain higher original-task accuracy than AdamW-goldilocks at equal weight norm. Xiaotian Zhang et al., 2026 ↗

Transfer and extrapolation

These studies ask when learned components help with new tasks and whether solutions work beyond the data used to evaluate them.

Learned components can accelerate new tasks 9 studies

Learned algorithmic components can transfer or compose to accelerate generalization. Transfer depends on the operation, representation and component position.

  • Transferring trained decoders accelerates multiplication; transferring embeddings lets three-operand addition reach the required test accuracy. Yeachan Park et al., 2024 ↗
Success on one split can hide extrapolation failures 7 studies

A learned algorithmic solution can succeed within its evaluation split yet fail on longer sequences, new formats or deeper compositions. Broader extrapolation depends on architecture and invariance training.

  • Text-rendered modular addition reaches 96.8% disjoint-pair accuracy but fails under position shifts and new templates. Nikolay Yudin, 2026 ↗

Measurement and interpretation

Complementary measurements and controls help track progress, test proposed explanations and distinguish correlation from causation.

Statistics can reveal progress before accuracy changes 23 studies

Weight, gradient, output and representation statistics can track or precede grokking and distinguish later overfitting. These signals do not by themselves identify a generalizing circuit.

  • Gradient-cascade dimension separates grokked and ungrokked ModAdd-59 trajectories 100–200 epochs before behavioral grokking. Pingao Wang, 2026 ↗
Early signals need controls 17 studies

A statistic that changes before grokking need not reliably predict it or explain its mechanism. Conclusions depend on null models, the coordinates used for analysis, the measurement window and whether interventions test what they are meant to test.

  • An eigenvalue-gap detector gives false alarms with short rolling windows in control runs without weight decay. Yongzhong Xu, 2026 ↗
Measurement changes how abrupt learning appears 14 studies

Accuracy thresholds, aggregation, plotting axes and evaluation procedures affect the apparent timing and suddenness of grokking. Measurements that vary continuously or separate component contributions can reveal a different trajectory.

  • POLCA projected-loss clusters better separate carry structure and reveal breakthroughs after the exact-loss plateau. Sara Kangaslahti et al., 2025 ↗
Complexity measures follow different trajectories 13 studies

Compression, curvature, parameter redundancy (degeneracy) and effective parameter count need not change together. A complexity measure can track training without anticipating generalization.

  • Reported local learning coefficient, a complexity measure, rises about fourfold before grokking, then plateaus during grokking. Tejas Pradeep Shirodkar et al., 2026 ↗
The transition type remains unresolved 13 studies

Statistical-physics accounts describe grokking through non-equilibrium dynamics, barrier crossing and finite-size transitions. The evidence does not establish a universal transition order or escape mechanism.

  • Extrapolated transition-type estimates vary across sampling grids, remaining inconclusive despite single-peaked distributions across seeds. Yu-Da Bi et al., 2026 ↗
Information and uncertainty follow distinct schedules 9 studies

Information, entropy and uncertainty measures can show peaks, reversals and compression phases around grokking. Their timing depends on the metric.

  • Under Gaussian VI, Bayesian linear regression shows growing accuracy and uncertainty-peak delays as λ approaches 1. Abdessamed Qchohi et al., 2026 ↗
Flatness alone does not ensure generalization 7 studies

Flatness can correlate with or modify grokking, but it is insufficient on its own. Flatness measures that change when the same model is expressed with different parameters need not determine when grokking starts.

  • Runs using only sharpness-aware minimization fail to generalize despite the lowest curvature by maximum Hessian eigenvalue. Mohnish Harwani, 2026 ↗

Where to start reading

  1. 1

    Alethea Power et al., 2022 ↗ Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets

    Establishes the original behavioral baseline: prolonged generalization delay after memorization on small algorithmic datasets.

  2. 2

    Neel Nanda et al., 2023 ↗ Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability

    Connects modular-addition grokking to Fourier computation, measurable progress before the test transition, and later sparsification.

  3. 3

    Chang Lu et al., 2026 ↗ Do Transformers Learn What Theory Predicts? Knowledge Representation-Guided Mechanistic Verification via Causal Abstraction

    Tests identifiable computation through causal abstraction beyond modular addition and challenges uniformly gradual circuit formation.

Known gaps in this draft

Open questions concern measuring the delay between memorization and generalization directly, reproducing results under matched conditions at scale, numerical effects, checking figures, study independence, and what norm and representation evidence reveals about mechanisms.

All 7 gaps
  • It remains unresolved whether shrinking the training set lengthens the gap after training accuracy saturates under fixed task and optimizer conditions. Time to a validation threshold does not establish that relationship.
  • Large-language-model studies use different definitions and protocols, leaving replication under matched conditions unresolved. Pretraining evidence relies on pairings chosen after the fact and evaluation after instruction tuning, while fine-tuning that injects facts includes failures to generalize.
  • It remains unclear how much numerical effects contribute to slingshots, the repeated sudden loss spikes late in training. Higher precision can remove spikes, and changing the order of floating-point sums can change whether individual runs grok.
  • Some conclusions about loss of generalization after reducing training data, algorithm differences across runs and the causes of loss spikes rest on training curves that could not be fully checked. The supporting figures were only partly accessible.
  • Some supporting studies share authors, may duplicate the same work, or measure an original study’s saved model again, so their independence remains unresolved. Several proposed generalizations still need confirmation from independent studies.
  • Disagreements about controlling weight magnitude remain hard to interpret because studies differ in when they project weights back to a chosen norm and in other experimental conditions. These comparisons do not yet isolate when controlling weight magnitude governs grokking.
  • The geometry of learned representations, embedding spectra (how variation is distributed across directions), and concentration at particular Fourier frequencies in the final model do not establish when a generalizing computation forms or whether runs learn different algorithms.
